chunks: Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Huzayfa ibn Mansur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Food supplies ran out in the era of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). So the Muslims came to him and said, 'O Messenger of Allah! The food has run out and there remains nothing of it except with so-and-so, so order him to sell it to the people.' He (peace be upon him) praised Allah and extolled Him, then said, 'O so-and-so! The Muslims have mentioned that the food has run out except for a small amount with you, so bring it out and sell it as you wish, and do not withhold it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on hoarding food and controlling prices during scarcity?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the Prophet’s authority to intervene in market mechanisms during scarcity, illustrating the concept of *al-man' al-ta'sir* (withholding goods to raise prices). While the Prophet permitted the owner to sell 'as he wished,' Shia jurists interpret this as a directive to prioritize public welfare over absolute profit maximization, forming a basis for price control (*tas'ir*) in times of crisis. The narration underscores the ethical obligation of wealth holders to prevent artificial scarcity, a principle central to Islamic economic jurisprudence.
